name: Contemporary Image Collective
funding: No funder list is published. The Arab Fund for Arts and Culture lists a 2024 CiC project under Egypt's National Cultural Opportunities Fund. Cairo artists depend on foreign grants.

name: Darb 1718 Contemporary Art and Culture Center
funding: Small non-profit mainly funded by artist Moataz Nasr. 2022 Moleskine Foundation grant. 2025 artist-donated auction at Tarathuna.

name: Museum of Modern Egyptian Art
funding: Owned by the Ministry of Culture.

name: Townhouse Gallery
funding: Small independent non-profit founded 1998 by William Wells, now a foundation; its website no longer resolves.

name: Art D'Égypte
funding: Private firm of Nadine Abdel Ghaffar. Egypt's foreign and tourism ministries and UNESCO sponsor Forever Is Now. Partners: LMD, Suez Canal Bank, BMW (2026); TotalEnergies, Afreximbank (2024).

name: Museo de la Palabra y la Imagen (MUPI)
funding: Private non-profit. AGIAMONDO and the Ford Foundation backed its 2026 archive move; gifts from citizens, the diaspora and firms repay the annexe mortgage. Its site lists no donors or budget.

name: Addis Foto Fest
funding: Produced by Desta for Africa, directed by Aida Muluneh. The last sponsor list is from 2018: Swiss Embassy, Canon, National Geographic Society, Marriott and others. None published since.

name: Zoma Museum
funding: Privately funded. Land bought from 2013 with Assegued's income as a curator and anthropologist and sales of Sime's artwork. Sime is represented by James Cohan Gallery, New York.

name: Listasavn Føroya (National Gallery of the Faroe Islands)
EMMA Espoo Museum of Modern Art
funding: City of Espoo, plus the Saastamoinen Foundation collection.

name: Siida Sámi Museum (Saamelaismuseo Siida)
funding: A small state-backed museum: most of its money comes from Finland's Ministry of Education and Culture, plus a yearly grant from Inari Municipality.

name: Villa Kokkonen
funding: The City of Järvenpää, owner since 1998, runs it. The first restoration phase, budgeted at EUR 425,000, drew on city investments and a EUR 105,000 culture ministry grant.
